newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich backs using US budget surplus to cut debt. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Gingrich backs using US budget surplus to cut debt. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: Speaker Newt Gingrich and some 95 other members of the House of Representatives introduced (corrects from "signed") a bill on Thursday that would direct future budget surpluses towards the retirement of federal debt, tax relief, and restoring solvency to federal trust funds.
"I believe that the broad-based support for balancing the budget translates into support for eliminating the national debt," Gingrich said in a statement.
"Not only will this bill ensure that we fully repay our debt, it establishes a clear priority for lowering taxes," he added.

The bill, called the National Debt Repayment Act, would divide any federal surplus into thirds. One-third would go towards tax relief, another third to pay back the Social Security Trust Fund, and the final third towards repaying the Highway Trust Fund, Superfund and other trust funds, said a spokesman for Rep. Mark Nuemann, (R-Wis), the bill's original sponsor.
The trust funds currently contain non-marketable Treasury securities which are effectively IOUs and would be replaced with marketable government securities.
"Because those trust funds hold obligations, if you pay those back you are paying down debt," the spokesman said. "The net effect is you are replacing an IOU with a real asset."
The measure calls for the Treasury to buy back government debt held by the public in order to place marketable government securities in the trust funds.

Assuming revenues grow at an annual 6.0 percent, the new measure will allow the government by 2002 to pay $112.6 billion to the Social Security fund, pay in full the $33.3 billion Highway fund plus pay $79 billion to other funds, and provide an additional $112.6 billion in tax cuts, Neumann's office said.
